response.report:
EXAM: Chest radiograph, one view, 2026-11-12
CLINICAL INDICATION: Routine surveillance. History of treated breast cancer. No new symptoms.
ORDERING PROVIDER: Dr. L. Okafor (synthetic), medical oncology
COMPARISON: Chest radiograph, 2026-02-10
TECHNIQUE: Current PA. Prior PA. Differences from prior: the current image has slightly higher contrast and penetration, and the breast shadows and left chest wall soft tissues lie differently. Both blind reads judged the studies comparable.

LOOK AT FIRST:
- F6: Right hilar and infrahilar fullness and density, more conspicuous than on the prior. Indeterminate. The reads disagreed (only 1 of 2 reads recorded it). Not time-sensitive. Triage: urgency high, no on-call page, radiologist review next shift.
- F2: Coarse linear markings in the right medial lower zone, more conspicuous than on the prior. Indeterminate. Both reads indeterminate. Not time-sensitive.

FINDINGS (systematic read, done blind to the indication):
- Airway / lungs: Trachea central with slight rightward deviation at the aortic arch, within normal. Carina and main bronchi not narrowed. Lungs well inflated. No consolidation, mass or band-like collapse. Coarse linear markings in the right medial lower zone are more conspicuous on the current (F2, indeterminate; the higher contrast and different breast shadow position on the current might explain this). A tiny dense focus projects over the right lower zone and is undetermined (see CAN'T DETERMINE). Vascular markings reach the chest wall on both sides.
- Mediastinum / hila: Aortic knuckle prominent, consistent with an unfolded aorta, similar to prior (F3). Upper mediastinum not widened. Right hilar and infrahilar fullness and density, more conspicuous than on the prior (F6). Indeterminate. The reads disagreed. Size change is not comparable, and no measurement is available. The left hilum is not enlarged. Note for resident: the systematic read text describes the hila as normal without one-sided enlargement, which conflicts with F6; please reconcile on the source images.
- Pleura: No pleural line to suggest pneumothorax. Right costophrenic angle sharp. Left costophrenic angle appears sharp and is partly overlapped by breast shadow. No visible pleural thickening.
- Heart: Cardiac silhouette within normal limits on PA, with clear borders, similar to prior (F4).
- Bones / soft tissue: No displaced rib fracture or destructive rib lesion seen at this resolution. Clavicles and shoulders intact. Mild curvature and degenerative change of the visible spine. Both breast shadows present. No soft tissue gas. Left chest wall implanted device with arcing tubing and a small metallic component over the left mid zone, consistent with an implanted venous access device, present on both studies (F1). No new device. The component projects over a higher rib level on the current. Upper abdomen: more gas-filled bowel loops in the left upper abdomen on the current (F5). Indeterminate. The reads disagreed (only 1 of 2 reads recorded it). No free gas under either dome.

INTERVAL CHANGE:
- Changed (apparent, not confirmed): F2 right lower zone markings more conspicuous, indeterminate, technique may account for it. F6 right hilar and infrahilar fullness more conspicuous, indeterminate, reads disagreed, not comparable. F5 more left upper abdominal bowel gas, indeterminate, reads disagreed. The left chest wall device component projects at a higher rib level on the current. Breast and chest wall positioning might explain this, and true migration cannot be judged.
- Unchanged: Prominent aortic knuckle with upper mediastinum not widened (F3). Cardiac silhouette (F4). Left chest wall implanted venous access device present on both studies, no new device (F1). No pneumothorax. No free gas under the diaphragm. Bones and soft tissues same appearance as prior.

RECIST 1.1: Not computed on radiographs. No confirmed measurements.

CAN'T DETERMINE:
- Is the tiny dense focus over the right lower zone on the current a true nodule, for example a calcified granuloma, or a vessel end-on? | Reason: The focus is very small, sits among crossing vessels, and is not clearly visible on the prior, which has lower contrast. A frontal film does not separate a small nodule from a vessel end-on or a bone island. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS. If it persists, CT chest.
- Is the increased conspicuity of the right lower zone markings a true interval change? (F2) | Reason: The current image has higher contrast and a different breast shadow position, both of which make markings look more prominent. | Recommend: Correlate clinically. Short-interval repeat PA and lateral, or CT chest if there is clinical concern.
- Where is the catheter tip of the left chest wall device, and has the device moved? (F1) | Reason: The central course of the tubing is not traceable through the mediastinum at this resolution. The metallic component projects at a different rib level on the two films, which soft tissue and breast positioning might explain. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS with windowing for lines. Add a lateral view if tip position matters clinically.
- Is there a small left pleural effusion or a subtle left lower zone opacity? | Reason: Breast shadow overlaps the left costophrenic region and lower zone on both films, and there is no lateral view. | Recommend: Lateral view if clinically relevant.
- Are there subtle lesions in the ribs or spine? | Reason: The images are low resolution and compressed, so fine bone detail such as pedicles and small lucent lesions is not assessable. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS on bone settings.
- Is the right hilar and infrahilar fullness a real interval change, such as enlarged nodes or a hilar mass, or prominent vessels made more conspicuous by technique? (F6) | Reason: A frontal film alone cannot separate vessels from nodes or mass. The current is sharper and at deeper inspiration than the prior. | Recommend: CT chest with contrast. A lateral view would help if CT is not immediately available.
- Is the small dense nodular focus over the medial right lower zone on the current a true lung nodule, a calcified granuloma, or a vessel seen end-on? | Reason: It is a small focus on X-ray within crowded bronchovascular markings and breast shadow, and no definite matching focus is seen at the same site on the softer prior image. | Recommend: CT chest.
- Are the more conspicuous right lower zone linear markings a true interstitial change? (F2) | Reason: The current is sharper and slightly different in exposure and inspiration, and breast shadow overlies the region on both films. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS. If the difference persists there, CT chest.
- Where is the port catheter tip, and has the port or catheter moved? (F1) | Reason: The catheter tip cannot be traced over the mediastinum at this image resolution. The different projected level of the reservoir may reflect arm and breast position only. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS with windowing to trace the catheter to its tip. Add a lateral view if tip position remains unclear.
- Is the heterogeneous texture of the left humeral head a bone lesion or a normal or degenerative appearance? | Reason: The images are low resolution and the shoulder is at the edge of a chest film, so fine bone detail is unreliable. The appearance is similar on both studies. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS. Dedicated left shoulder radiographs if the appearance persists.

IMPRESSION:
1. Right hilar and infrahilar fullness and density, more conspicuous than on the prior (F6). Indeterminate, and the reads disagreed. It could be a real change or technique (sharper image, deeper inspiration). A frontal film cannot separate vessels from nodes or mass. Prior breast cancer history flagged for earlier human review.
2. More conspicuous coarse linear markings in the right medial lower zone (F2). Indeterminate. Technique and breast shadow position might explain it.
3. Tiny dense focus over the right lower zone, undetermined (nodule versus vessel end-on).
4. Left chest wall implanted venous access device present on both studies, no new device (F1). Catheter tip and any migration cannot be determined.
5. More left upper abdominal bowel gas (F5). Indeterminate, and the reads disagreed. No free gas under the diaphragm.
6. Not assessable on these films: small left pleural effusion or left lower zone opacity (breast shadow, no lateral), subtle rib or spine lesions, and left humeral head texture.
7. No definite lung mass, confluent opacity, right pleural effusion or destructive rib lesion. Upper mediastinum not widened. Aortic knuckle (F3) and cardiac silhouette (F4) similar to prior.

RECOMMENDATIONS:
- CT chest with contrast for the right hilar fullness (F6) and the right lower zone focus. The interval is not specified in the findings and is to be set by the reviewing radiologist. A lateral view if CT is not immediately available.
- Review source images in PACS: right lower zone markings (F2), the dense focus, catheter tip tracing with line windowing, bone settings, and the left humeral head. If the F2 difference persists, CT chest. If concern remains, short-interval repeat PA and lateral.
- Lateral view if the left pleural region or catheter tip position is clinically relevant.
- Dedicated left shoulder radiographs if the humeral head appearance persists.

AI DRAFT: requires resident review and attending signature.
